worktrees.bootstrap: symlink .env and .env.local from the main checkout's apps/api/ into the worktree's apps/api/, then poetry install (apps/api) and bun install (root). The plugin's worktree-bootstrap.sh does all three.

local-db.label: local Supabase stack
local-db.notes: One stack for every worktree. A reset rebuilds from the resetting worktree's migrations alone, so it drops any migration another branch applied until that branch re-runs `supabase migration up --local`. `db-reset-local` refuses when the stack holds a migration this worktree lacks; `db-reset-local-anyway` is the override and is what a slot is for. One full reset per branch, at PR-ready time; prove DDL on a scratch database before that.

api-port.label: API server on port 8000
api-port.notes: Every serve task binds 8000; one API server across all worktrees. `uvicorn main:app --port <other>` sidesteps the slot but then nothing that calls the API finds it; say so in the request if you do it.

hosted.label: hosted Supabase project
hosted.notes: Reads, credentials and writes on the hosted project are Jason's to run: the classifier refuses production reads from a session and that refusal is correct. A session asks mission control for a hosted window (read-only, announced, nobody else reading during a cold-cache measurement) and asks Jason for the exact command. A hosted write is never a development step.

commands.test: cd apps/api && poetry run poe test
commands.lint: cd apps/api && poetry run poe lint
commands.schema: cd apps/api && poetry run poe schema

facts: Changelog entries are written on main after a PR merges and its tag lands, never on a branch; put the intended wording in the PR description instead.
Env files: the real `.env` and `.env.local` live at the repository root and are symlinked into `apps/api/`; a worktree gets the same two symlinks from the bootstrap.
Every `poe` task runs as `poetry run poe <task>` from `apps/api/`; `-hosted` loads `.env`, `-local` loads `.env` then `.env.local`.
Contract regeneration: `bun run contract` from the repository root after any route or response-model change, docstrings included; commit both generated files; on a conflict rerun, never hand-merge.
Feature work reaches main through a pull request; a roadmap or Jira sync commit goes straight on main and must re-render the dashboard in the same commit or every open PR's CI goes red.
A stack lives in one worktree; `gh stack merge <pr#> --merge` lands a layer and everything below it; never `git merge main` into a layer.
Shared SQL functions: one author per function per migration, a redefinition pastes the whole body, the second to merge rewrites from main, migration timestamps are assigned at kick-off.
human_gates: hosted credentials (an API key, an invite)
gh stack merge, gh pr merge
